subject: Dedicated reservation blueprint and ramp options for NovaPulse
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@novapulse.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation blueprint and ramp options for NovaPulse

Alex —

Great to meet yesterday. As discussed, I put together three reservation paths for NovaPulse that map to your Q3 latency targets and projected throughput. The attached spreadsheet has cost and utilization projections but the quick summary below should help drive the internal decision.

Option A — Conservative steady-state
- Minimum GPU floor: 8 GPUs (NVIDIA H200-like perf)
- Peak cluster size: 12 GPUs (autoscale with reserved burst)
- Ramp: Activate 4 GPUs month 1, add 4 month 3, finish to 12 by month 6
- Use case: predictable production traffic, lower orchestration risk

Option B — Aggressive growth with burst credits
- Minimum GPU floor: 4 GPUs
- Peak cluster size: 20 GPUs (burst to accommodate seasonal spikes)
- Ramp: 4 -> 8 (M1) -> 14 (M2) -> 20 (M4) with temporary burst credits for M2
- Use case: teams prioritizing cost-efficiency while accepting more variance in latency during spikes

Option C — Hybrid warm pool + cold reserve
- Minimum GPU floor: 2 warm GPUs + 16 cold standby (fast-attach within SLA window)
- Peak cluster size: 18 active (when cold pool is warmed)
- Ramp: Warm pool available month 1; cold attach phased to reach full capacity by month 4
- Use case: strict cost control with planned scheduled workloads and occasional high-concurrency jobs

Key operational controls we recommend across all options:
- Prefix KV caching for your common prompts (reduces token compute by ~25% in our sims)
- Two-tier model routing: default cheaper variant for inference, higher-capacity variant for tail-latency SLOs
- Canary rollout: start new model versions on 1 GPU and expand after QA metrics pass

Attachments: novapulse-dedicated-options.xlsx (spreadsheet), novapulse-map-v1.2.pdf (architecture map)

Next steps: if you can confirm your preferred ramp aggressiveness and procurement timelines, we’ll convert one of these into a formal Dedicated proposal and lock pricing for the quarter.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation blueprint and ramp options for NovaPulse

Jordan —

Saw your options. A couple quick notes from an ops sizing perspective:
- If they plan realtime chat + batch embeddings at scale, Option A's 8 GPU floor is the safer baseline to avoid repeated cold-start warmups.
- For Option B we should quantify the burst credit usage explicitly in the sheet (add a burst-cost line item per month).
- Option C: include documented attach-time SLA (we recommend 3–5 min attach for cold standbys to be contractually explicit).

I annotated the spreadsheet with per-GPU throughput assumptions (see sheet tab "throughput_assumptions").

Also, can we add a one-page runnable rollout checklist for their SREs (model pins, KV cache TTLs, rollout windows)? I can draft it and attach to the formal proposal.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@novapulse.ai>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@novapulse.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation blueprint and ramp options for NovaPulse

Jordan / Ben —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifying questions from our end:
1) For Option C, when you say "cold standby", what instance of autoscaler are you using and how do you guarantee the attach window? We have an internal compliance requirement to keep tail-latency under 500ms for interactive flows.
2) Can you confirm the SLA uptime associated with each option and what credit/penalty structure we get if we miss the SLO?
3) Procurement: we need an expected contract milestone schedule (PO issuance, invoice cadence, onboarding kickoff) to sync with finance.

We'd like a single-page summary for leadership that clarifies cost delta between Option A and Option B over 12 months and a recommended default if we want to prioritize latency over cost.

I'll loop in Billing if needed but attaching Procurement to keep timelines tight.

Regards,
Alex Soto
Head of ML Platforms | NovaPulse
alex.soto@novapulse.ai

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation blueprint and ramp options for NovaPulse

Alex / team —

Thanks for the questions — below are concrete answers we will include in the formal proposal and SOW:

1) Cold standby attach and tail-latency guarantees
- Cold standby uses our fast-attach block with pre-provisioned images in the same region; empirical attach window is 2–5 minutes dependent on model size. For interactive-critical routes we recommend keeping a small warm pool (2–4 GPUs) to ensure sub-500ms tail-latency. We'll document the attach procedure and mitigation steps in the SRE checklist.

2) SLA and credits
- Standard Dedicated SLA: 99.9% monthly availability for active cluster capacity.
- If monthly availability drops below SLA, credits are applied on a sliding scale: 99.9%–99.5% = 5% credit; 99.5%–99.0% = 10% credit; <99.0% = 20% credit. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate higher SLA targets.

3) Procurement milestone schedule (sample)
- Week 0: PO issuance (customer)
- Week 1: Contract countersign and invoice for initial onboarding fee
- Week 2: Onboarding kickoff (technical deep dive)
- Week 4–8: Staged activation and validation windows per selected ramp path

Action items I will do by EOD Friday:
- Produce the one-page leadership cost delta (Option A vs B vs C) over 12 months
- Add burst-cost line items and attach-time SLA into the spreadsheet
- Draft a 1-page SRE rollout checklist for you to share with engineering

If Procurement can share target PO date we'll align pricing lock windows.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
